name: Roman Chamomile
source_reference: Arctander, 'Perfume and Flavor Materials of Natural Origin', 1960; ISO 5765-1:2002; Carnat et al., Flavour and Fragrance Journal, 2004
notes: Roman chamomile is ester-rich and fruity, very different from German chamomile (Matricaria recutita) which is dominated by chamazulene (blue color). Roman chamomile oil is one of the most expensive essential oils due to low yield (~0.5-1%).

key_markers.7779-81-9: Isobutyl angelate - dominant ester defining Roman chamomile's sweet-fruity character
key_markers.53398-85-9: 2-Methylbutyl angelate - characteristic angelic acid ester contributing to apple-like note
key_markers.30460-92-5: Pinocarvone - bicyclic ketone providing herbaceous depth

olfactive_description: Sweet, fruity-herbaceous with a distinctive warm apple-like ester character. Soft, comforting, and rounded with a slightly green-herbal undertone. Lacks the sharp medicinal quality of German chamomile.
